newsitem.title: USA: Chromalloy Gas sues United Tech. in patent dispute.
newsitem.headline: Chromalloy Gas sues United Tech. in patent dispute.

text.p: Chromalloy Gas Turbine Corp has sued United Technologies Corp for making and selling airfoils that allegedly infringe two patents owned by Chromalloy.

In papers filed in the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Chromalloy said United's Pratt & Whitney division, in East Hartford, Conn, allegedly used a method for making cooling holes in airfoils covered by Chromalloy patents '785 and '486.
The suit seeks an order blocking further alleged infringement and unspecified damages tripled for intentional infringement.

Chromalloy is based in San Antonio, Texas and repairs aircraft engine parts. According to company spokesman Jim Grossman, an anti-trust trial in a Texas state court against Pratt & Whitney is expected to end sometime in November.

Chromalloy, which is seeking compensatory damages of approximately $150 million, alleged in court papers in the Texas case that United was trying to eliminate "competing sources of repairs...(and block) the use of...better and/or less expensive repair procedures."
